grades.quote: When a trap is taken into S-mode, `sepc` is written with the virtual address of the instruction that was interrupted or that encountered the exception.
grades.reason: Directly states that on a trap into S-mode, sepc is written with the virtual address of the interrupted or faulting instruction. It also says SRET implicitly reads sepc, which covers how the saved address is used.

grades.quote: hardware records the PC that triggered the exception here.
grades.reason: The passage covers both parts of the query for LoongArch debug exceptions only. DERA records the PC that triggered the exception, and ERTN fetches the return address from it when CSR.DBG.DM=1. It doesn't cover the general exception return address register (ERA) or other exception types, so it answers only part of the query.
A CSR address table that lists exception return address registers (TLBRERA, MERRERA) by name only. It gives no detail on what is saved or how it is used, so it is limited auxiliary information.
About thread context switching in xv6 (swtch saving ra and callee-saved registers). It does not cover the saved program counter after an exception.
